description: Phaser 3 framework layer — Phaser.Game bootstrap + a single MainScene with arcade physics, a bouncing sprite, and cursor-key input wired from first render.

buildHints.whenToUse: 2D browser games — platformers, arcade, tower defense, match-3, tile-based roguelikes. Pick this over three.js when the primary surface is a 2D canvas with sprites + physics, not 3D geometry.
firstSteps: Run `pnpm install` then `pnpm dev` — Vite serves on 5173 with HMR; the bouncing ball renders immediately.
Add new scenes under `src/scenes/` and register them in the `scene` array of the Phaser.Game config in `src/main.ts`.
Put art assets in `public/assets/` and load them with `this.load.image('key', 'assets/foo.png')` inside a Scene's `preload()`.
Arcade physics is enabled by default — attach a physics body via `this.physics.add.sprite(x, y, key)`.
Run `pnpm build` to emit static assets to `dist/` — deploy to any static host.
gotchas: `this` inside `preload/create/update` is the Scene, not the Game. If you extract callbacks, bind or use arrow functions — losing `this` silently breaks asset loading.
Phaser clamps `update(time, delta)` delta — never assume 1/60 s between frames on throttled tabs. Always scale movement by `delta / 1000`.
Sprite textures are cached by key — loading the same key twice is a no-op after the first load. Use distinct keys per asset or call `this.textures.remove(key)` before reloading.
Canvas size is controlled by the Phaser.Game config `scale` property, NOT CSS. Setting CSS width/height stretches the canvas and breaks pointer coordinates.
Phaser ships its own TypeScript declarations; no `@types/phaser` package is needed or available.
architectureNotes: One Phaser.Game instance per page. Scenes are the unit of composition — add, switch, pause, resume via `this.scene.*`.
Keep game state in the Scene (or a Scene's `registry`); do NOT attach it to `window`/global. Scene transitions clear local state.

placeholders.description: Default scene with a bouncing sprite + cursor-key input. Replace the graphics-generated ball + logic with your actual game loop; keep the scene lifecycle hooks (preload/create/update).
Phaser.Game config with arcade physics and FIT scaling. Adjust width/height, gravity, and the scene array as the game grows.
